result.title: A research world model of power engineering learns its dynamics and reveals what-ifs
result.summary: Decisions about the direction of research in power engineering determine which technologies mature and, through them, shape infrastructure that lasts decades, yet their consequences cannot be observed before they are taken, and existing forecasts of research fields extrapolate a single trajectory. Here we introduce research world models, which treat a research field as a dynamical system that can be acted upon, and establish one for power engineering from 1.1 million papers. A distilled language model reads each paper into role-typed concepts, two sophisticated, high-fidelity graph-temporal neural network cores learn how the resulting concept network evolves, and operators learned from natural experiments in the publication record estimate the effects of interventions. In temporally held-out tests, the model forecast years ahead which concepts would grow and which method-target pairs would be joined for the first time, outperforming tuned machine-learning baselines in most settings, and its estimated intervention effects tracked those realized in natural experiments it had not seen. Its training scheme and three of its operators replicated in two fields withheld from development. Questions posed in natural language are compiled by a domain-specialized 27-billion-parameter language model into executable actions and answered as paired simulations with and without the intervention. The answers were rated 4.1 of 5 for faithfulness by an independent language-model judge. By revealing the latent dynamics of a research field and its response to interventions, research world models offer a new way to simulate and test research decisions before they are made.

AI.brief_summary: 该文用蒸馏语言模型把 110 万篇电力工程论文读成角色化概念，用图-时序网络学习概念网络的演化，并从发表记录中的自然实验学习干预算子，从而在自然语言问答下做「干预/不干预」配对模拟与预测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「隐动态建模＋干预算子＋配对反事实模拟」可能为 LVR 中推理状态如何更新、以及如何评估 latent 内容的因果作用提供类比框架，但对象是文献网络而非视觉证据，迁移需较多核查。
